newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Chretien welcomes Clinton re-election.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien welcomes Clinton re-election.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Wednesday he would call U.S. President Bill Clinton to congratulate him on his re-election, but would also press him on friction between the two countries over Cuba.

Chretien said he expected to speak with Clinton later on Wednesday and would use the opportunity to raise some of the problems between Ottawa and Washington, including the controversial Helms-Burton law on Cuba.
Chretien said Clinton's re-election would make the relationship between the two countries easier.
"We have worked with him for the last three years so it's kind of easier to carry on with an administration that you know the main players," Chretien told reporters.

"For him it's a great achievement to be re-elected. I will be talking briefly to him and I will probably mention some of the problems that have to be dealt with," Chretien said, indicating Helms-Burton would be on that agenda.
The Helms-Burton law, named after its U.S. congressional sponsors, punishes foreign investors for doing business with Cuba.

Canada has challenged the legislation under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and has joined a European Union complaint to the World Trade Organization. It also adopted its own legislation in retaliation.

International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said he hoped that with the election behind him, Clinton would agree to extend his six-month suspension of a key provision of the Helms-Burton bill, and this time do it for a longer period.

The suspended provision, Title III, allows U.S. citizens and companies to sue in U.S. courts foreign investors using property in Cuba which was confiscated after the Fidel Castro's 1959 Communist revolution.
Canadian Foreign Affairs Minister Lloyd Axworthy said it was too early to tell if Clinton's re-election would have any impact on the Helms-Burton law.
"We have good relations with Mr. Clinton and now we can address some of the important problems that have been pending until the election was over," Axworthy said.
